breakerPlatform.notes: Leviton load centers use proprietary plug-on LB-series breakers. Hot and neutral conductors land on panel lugs, not on the breaker itself. Not interchangeable with Square D / Eaton / Siemens breakers.

suffixKey.-T: current-generation standard thermal-magnetic (supersedes the un-suffixed LBxxx hydraulic-magnetic parts)
suffixKey.-S / -ST: Smart (1st gen / 2nd gen) metering + remote trip

smartUpgradePath.notes: 2nd-gen smart breakers are the drop-in metering replacements for the standard -T parts in these same slots.

openQuestions.recorded: 50A 2-pole double oven at Panel B slots 2/4
openQuestions.observed: 30A 2-pole generator inlet under a mechanical interlock plate
openQuestions.resolution: SAFETY-RELEVANT, NOW FIXED. The previous Panel B walkthrough told the operator to shut off 2/4 as the 'double oven' - 2/4 is the inlet breaker, and the real oven would have stayed energized behind a 30A feed. The oven is reassigned to 14/16 pending confirmation. The directory also reads 'Oven' at 5/7, but 5 and 7 are physically empty; confirm which is the live oven circuit.

openQuestions.observed: An installed black 2-pole-width device with no visible branding, handle or amp rating
openQuestions.resolution: Photograph straight-on to identify. Directory says 'Furn', which would fit a heat-pump air handler with resistance heat strips. Until identified its amp rating is unknown, it is in no shed list, and it contributes 0 W to the Panel B load figure - so that figure is optimistic by an unknown and potentially large margin.

openQuestions.recorded: Panel B connected load computes from recorded circuits only
openQuestions.observed: Three Panel B devices totalling 100A of breaker capacity have no circuits recorded
openQuestions.resolution: The Panel B load meter reads far lower than reality. B-6-8 (unknown, 'Furn'), B-10-12 (40A A/C) and B-28-30 (20A surge) all contribute 0 W. Do not trust the Panel B figure until these are traced. The Panel A figure is sound.
VERIFY BEFORE RELYING ON THIS. Either the AC is not on 23/25, or it is a much smaller unit than 3500W. A 3500W condenser would not run on a 20A 2-pole.

openQuestions.observed: Female L14-30 twist-lock face on the wall left of Panel A
openQuestions.resolution: VERIFY. A female receptacle would require a male-to-male cord from the Anker's L14-30 output, which is neither safe nor code-compliant. Confirm whether this is actually a flanged power inlet (male pins) before the first real transfer.

HYPOTHESIS: the 80-gallon electric water heater. It is in the unfinished basement (see the A-30 circuit note), a resistance tank that size is normally 30A 2-pole, and a water heater is exactly what you would tape for load shedding. Test by killing 19/21 and checking for hot water.

openQuestions.recorded: 'Mud Room Air Conditioner' on Panel A 23/25
openQuestions.observed: A 23/25 is a 20A 2-pole; B 10/12 is a 40A 2-pole the directory calls A/C
openQuestions.resolution: Determine whether there are two cooling units. B 10/12 fits a main heat pump condenser. A 23/25 at 20A would fit a mini-split or small unit.

openQuestions.recorded: 120V circuits on slots 7, 10, 13 and 15, which are also halves of 2-pole breakers
openQuestions.observed: Slots 5/7, 10/12 and 13/15 each carry a single 2-pole device
openQuestions.resolution: Most likely multi-wire branch circuits: two 120V legs sharing a neutral under a common-trip 2-pole handle. A 1974 house would commonly do this for kitchen counter circuits (10/12 fits the counter + dishwasher entries) and for bedroom/lighting runs. If so these are not 240V loads at all. Confirm by checking for a shared neutral at the panel.

openQuestions.observed: Breakers installed with no endpoints traced
openQuestions.resolution: Still fully unidentified in Panel A: 19/21 (30A), 27/29 (20A). A-23-25 has a load recorded but the amperage contradicts it. A-5-7 has circuits on slot 7 only - the other leg is untraced.
Unmapped 120V circuit - blank on the directory card and absent from the walkthrough. Test it against the four entries in unassignedEndpoints.

openQuestions.recorded: Handwritten directory cards in both panels
openQuestions.observed: The Panel B card lists an oven at 5/7 (physically empty), a washer at 11 (the walkthrough puts it on A-9), and has no entry for slot 26
openQuestions.resolution: Treat this file as authoritative and the cards as historical. Both cards should be reprinted from this data.

safetyWarnings.title: Disconnect Trickle Charger
safetyWarnings.message: BEFORE starting: Unplug the Anker F3800+ from its 120V trickle charge outlet.

safetyWarnings.title: Main Breaker First
safetyWarnings.message: Always turn OFF the main breaker BEFORE engaging the generator/backup inlet breaker.

safetyWarnings.title: Interlock Safety
safetyWarnings.message: The interlock prevents the main breaker and generator inlet from being ON simultaneously. Never attempt to bypass this.

safetyWarnings.title: 2-Pole Breakers Are Common Trip
safetyWarnings.message: Slots 5/7, 10/12, 13/15, 19/21, 23/25 and 27/29 in Panel A each share one handle. Switching one slot off switches both. Plan shed lists by device, not by slot number.

panelA.title: Unplug Anker Trickle Charger
panelA.instruction: Locate the Anker F3800+ and unplug it from the 120V wall outlet it uses for trickle charging.
panelA.warning: This must be done BEFORE connecting to the panel.

panelA.title: Turn Off High-Draw Breakers
panelA.instruction: At Panel A, turn OFF these breakers to prevent overloading the Anker:

panelA.title: Turn Off Main Breaker
panelA.instruction: Flip the MAIN breaker at Panel A to the OFF position.
panelA.warning: This disconnects your home from the grid.

panelA.title: Connect Anker to Panel
panelA.instruction: Connect the Anker F3800+ output cable to the generator inlet on the wall immediately left of Panel A.

panelA.title: Engage Generator Inlet Breaker
panelA.instruction: Slide the interlock plate and flip the 30A 2-pole generator inlet breaker (Panel A slots 2/4, top of the right column) to ON. The interlock should now allow this since the main is OFF.

panelA.title: Turn On Anker
panelA.instruction: Power on the Anker F3800+. Panel A circuits (except those turned off) should now have power.

panelA.title: Verify Critical Loads
panelA.instruction: Check that the refrigerator, sump pump, and internet are working.

panelB.title: Position the Truck
panelB.instruction: Park the F-150 Lightning near the outdoor 30A receptacle.

panelB.title: Turn Off High-Draw Breakers
panelB.instruction: At Panel B, turn OFF these breakers:
panelB.warning: CORRECTED: an earlier version listed slots 2/4 here as the double oven. 2/4 is the GENERATOR INLET and must stay available - do not switch it off.

panelB.title: Turn Off Main Breaker
panelB.instruction: Flip the MAIN breaker at Panel B to the OFF position.

panelB.title: Connect Truck to Receptacle
panelB.instruction: Using the truck's bed-mounted 30A power outlet, connect to the outdoor receptacle with the appropriate cable.

panelB.title: Enable Pro Power Onboard
panelB.instruction: In the truck, enable Pro Power Onboard and select the appropriate output level.

panelB.title: Engage Generator Inlet Breaker
panelB.instruction: Flip the generator inlet breaker at Panel B to ON.
panelB.warning: Slots 2/4, top of the right column, under the interlock plate. The outdoor receptacle configuration is not yet confirmed - check it before the first real transfer.

panelB.title: Verify Panel B Loads
panelB.instruction: Check that Panel B circuits are receiving power.

rechargeAnkerFromTruck.title: Check Anker Battery Level
rechargeAnkerFromTruck.instruction: If the Anker F3800+ is running low, you can recharge it from the Lightning.

rechargeAnkerFromTruck.title: Connect Charging Cable
rechargeAnkerFromTruck.instruction: Connect a charging cable from one of the truck's outlets to the Anker's AC input.

rechargeAnkerFromTruck.title: Monitor Charging
rechargeAnkerFromTruck.instruction: The Anker can charge while also providing backup power (pass-through charging).

metadata.notes: Device-first schema. One entry per physical breaker; circuits nest underneath. Shed lists live on devices via shedIn so common-trip behaviour is explicit and there is one source of truth. Handwritten panel directory cards are historical, not authoritative.

changelog.summary: Panel B photo inventory: 10 devices, all 30 slots reconciled (16 occupied, 14 empty). Slots 2/4 identified as the generator inlet - previously recorded as a 50A double oven, which put the inlet on the Panel B shed list. Oven reassigned to 14/16. B-1-3 40A->50A, B-13 15A->20A. One unidentified device at B 6/8. Circuits now carry verified / verificationMethod. Added unassignedEndpoints and panels.*.emptySlots; dropped slotsSurveyed (now derived from slot reconciliation). Resolved open questions retired to this changelog.

Moved to blackstart repo. Shed lists derived from devices[].shedIn (dropped scenarios.shedDevices/shedDeviceLabels). Added panels.*.slotsSurveyed and a Panel B generatorInlet stub. Rewrote auto-generated device labels. Panel B walkthrough shed list now scenario-derived.
Restructured to device-first. Panel A hardware photo-verified; Panel B carried forward unverified.

Panel A physical breaker inventory from photos. Corrected amps on slots 8, 13/15, 14, 17, 18, 19/21, 23/25. Identified slots 2/4 as the generator inlet breaker under a mechanical interlock. Flagged slots 5/7, 10/12, 13/15 as probable MWBCs.
